related_synthesis_entries.claim: The general recipe of choosing a contour kernel is useful only when remote edges vanish, residues and zero corrections are computable, and the resulting correction is identifiable; the failed modulus transfer illustrates a concrete tractability boundary.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical work is done by the contour weight: its decay removes the remote sides of a rectangle, while its behavior on the vertical line selects a weighted component of log-zeta. The new odd-in-t kernels redirect the earlier log-modulus construction toward arg-zeta.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source recalls integrating log zeta against g(z)=1/(a^2-(z-b)^2) around a rectangle based at Re z=b, with the three remote-edge integrals vanishing as the rectangle expands. It then announces two families of integrals of t arg(zeta(b+it)) against rational denominators.
directed.conceptual_reading: A criterion is engineered by choosing a kernel that both controls the contour and projects the desired boundary observable. Here changing the parity and pole structure of the weight moves attention from log-modulus to phase without changing the contour-residue architecture.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The complex logarithm on z=b+it decomposes into log modulus and argument; the weighted vertical-boundary integral is then bridged by residue and generalized Littlewood formulas to poles and zeros inside the rectangle.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This span motivates rather than performs the new constructions. The log branch and argument convention occur later, remote-edge decay is cited rather than proved here, and the displayed formulas are OCR-fragmented.
directed.uncertainty: High confidence in the design pattern and target integral families; low confidence in reconstructing any exact criterion or admissible parameter range from this introductory span alone.

supported: The span recalls the rectangular-contour construction, identifies the left-edge weighted log-zeta integral, states that the three remote-edge integrals vanish as the rectangle expands, and invokes residue and generalized Littlewood analysis.
It explicitly announces two rationally weighted t arg-zeta integral families as the new target.
inference: Kernel choice can reasonably be read as jointly controlling contour decay and which boundary component is observed.
unsupported_or_imported: The candidate presents 'new odd-in-t kernels' and a changed 'parity and pole structure' as an established contour construction, but this introductory span displays the target integrals without defining the new contour weights or deriving their component-selection behavior.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The criterion-engineering language is useful only if kept subordinate to the concrete contour facts; otherwise it becomes a generic 'kernel exposes structure' template.
context_or_ocr_risk: The displayed rational formulas are fragmented, and neither the complex-log branch nor the argument convention is fixed in this span.
missed_mechanism: The span motivates the phase-integral program but does not itself show how an imaginary-part or parity calculation produces either announced family.
revision_instructions: Retain the remote-edge-decay and announced target-integral claims, but recast parity, new pole structure, and phase projection as hypotheses to be established by the subsequent construction rather than facts proved by this span.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Resolvent-like zero sums generate a parameterized Volchkov family
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Replacing the original reciprocal quadratic zero weight by a shifted resolvent sum yields another closed-form zero identity and, through the same N(x) integration, a family identified with Theorem 2 at b equals one half.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Finite-cutoff tests compare convergence across criteria and parameters
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The authors report matched small discrepancies for three argument-integral identities, examine improvement as b approaches the known zero-free border, and separately test the principal-value modulus identity, providing diagnostics of numerical behavior rather than proof.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Integration by parts, pole cancellation, the zero-counting function, and the integrated argument transform the same contour information among weighted arg-zeta integrals, log-modulus integrals, and sums over zeros, explaining the correspondence among named criteria.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Each transformation carries distinct convergence, principal-value, branch, or quoted-theorem assumptions; equivalence of representations does not make them equally tractable numerically or analytically.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Argument, modulus, and zero sums are linked representations

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The source treats Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor as two output representations of one contour identity: differentiation and integration transforms move between an argument criterion and a log-modulus criterion without changing the underlying zero correction.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The span reproduces an earlier weighted log-modulus identity with an explicit sum over zeros to the right of b and recalls that the current argument equality follows from that theorem. At b=1/2, the transformed equality gives Volchkov's nested modulus form, while the earlier theorem gives the Balazard-Saias-Yor integral of log|zeta(1/2+it)|/(1/4+t^2)=0; the authors conclude that the two RH criteria are the same criterion differently written.
directed.conceptual_reading: Criterion identity is located in the invariant zero-accounting mechanism rather than in surface form. Distinct observables can be equivalent when a controlled transformation carries both the baseline and every off-line-zero correction between them.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Parameter differentiation, integration by parts, and Littlewood's relation form the bridge between the weighted log-modulus identity, the arg-zeta criterion, and the nested horizontal-modulus representation.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The original proof of the reproduced theorem is outside this source, and the unification depends on transformations developed in earlier spans with their convergence and branch assumptions. Same criterion means equivalent zero diagnostic, not identical integrands or equal numerical conditioning.
directed.uncertainty: The source's representation-level unification is explicit, but its validity is conditional on the quoted prior theorem and the analytic legitimacy of the intervening transforms.

supported: The span reproduces the earlier weighted log-modulus identity with an explicit sum over zeros to the right of b and states that current equality (6) is its direct consequence.
It states that at b=1/2 the current and prior notes yield the Volchkov and Balazard-Saias-Yor criteria respectively, and concludes that they are one criterion in different forms.
inference: The reproduced zero sum supports interpreting the unification as preservation of a common zero diagnostic, conditional on the claimed direct-consequence relation.
unsupported_or_imported: The candidate's specific bridge by parameter differentiation, integration by parts, and Littlewood's relation is not present in this exact span; it imports derivational details from earlier units.
The claim that the transformed b=1/2 equality itself 'gives Volchkov's nested modulus form' needs the preceding derivation and is not established by this remark alone.
